claims.text: Gate mode writes nothing, so unlike drift.check it cannot create the baseline it is missing -- and a gate reporting OK against nothing is the exact failure this subsystem exists to prevent.
claims.why: The claim refers to behaviour of drift.check which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Default: print what moved BEFORE re-baselining. Re-baselining is Tier 2 acceptance from drift.py, and Tier 2 only has teeth if a human sees it.

claims.text: The SAME analysis the page was rendered from. Re-scanning here would bank a tree that is a few seconds older than the one just published.

claims.text: The feature census, from the SAME reports, for the same reason: it used to be typed by hand and it was thirty commits stale while the picker read it as the top of the work queue. Generating it here is what makes 'it cannot be older than the run that produced it' true rather than intended.

observations.what: main() returns 0 on success, 1 on failure for --accept and --check; default mode always returns 0.
inventory_mod is imported locally inside main() to avoid circular imports or lazy loading.
The --check mode prints gate text and checks baseline existence; if no baseline, it prints a message and returns 1.
Default mode prints gate text, loads narrative, writes map, refreshes drift snapshot, and refreshes inventory.
